entries.title: Saju cafes
entries.content: In Seoul neighborhoods like Hongdae, saju and tarot cafes let friends get readings over coffee. It's a social outing, like a photo booth.
entries.source: Best of Korea: Saju reading guide
entries.label: Culture - education

entries.title: Saju in K-dramas
entries.content: K-dramas often use gunghap (compatibility) and fortune tellers as plot twists, such as a family checking a couple's charts before a wedding.
entries.source: Sajumuse blog: K-Pop and K-Drama Saju
entries.label: Culture - education

entries.title: 'Palja' in everyday speech
entries.content: Saju is short for saju palja, 'four pillars, eight characters'. Koreans say 'palja ga joa' (lucky in life) in daily talk.
entries.label: Culture - education

entries.title: Tojeong Bigyeol (토정비결)
entries.content: A New Year fortune book from the 1500s. Many Koreans read their Tojeong Bigyeol for fun around Lunar New Year.
entries.label: Culture - education

entries.title: Your 'tti' (띠)
entries.content: Koreans often ask 'what's your tti?' (your birth animal) to compare ages. It's the year pillar's animal, starting at Ipchun.
entries.label: Culture - education
